title: Comments of the Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance re the Preliminary Permit Application of DeepGreen Western Passage SPV, LLC re the DeepGreen Project under P-15424.

UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
             BEFORE THE FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


DeepGreen Western Passage SPV, LLC                                                             )
                                                                                               )

                                                                           ) Project No. 15424-000

                         COMMENTS OF THE
          ALASKA COMMERCIAL FISHERIES CONSERVATION ALLIANCE


The Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance ("ACFCA") respectfully submits these

comments in the above-captioned proceeding concerning the preliminary permit application of

DeepGreen Western Passage SPV, LLC ("DeepGreen Western Passage") for a proposed

underwater data center and marine hydrokinetic project in the Western Passage off Eastport,

Maine. ACFCA is not a resident of, and does not claim any direct interest in, the waters at issue in

this proceeding. ACFCA submits these comments solely to bring to the Commission's attention

information from a related proceeding that ACFCA believes may be relevant to the Commission's

consideration of this application.

I. ACFCA'S INTEREST

ACFCA is a nonprofit organization representing Upper Cook Inlet commercial fishing permit

holders in Alaska. ACFCA is an intervenor and protestant in FERC Docket No. P-15423-000,

concerning a preliminary permit application filed by DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV, LLC

("DeepGreen Cook Inlet") for a proposed underwater data center and marine hydrokinetic turbine

array in Upper Cook Inlet, Alaska. ACFCA understands that DeepGreen Cook Inlet and

DeepGreen Western Passage are both subsidiaries of DeepGreen Holdings LLC, managed by

Louis Wolfson, and that both entities were incorporated in Delaware in January 2026, using

substantially similar project designs, equipment references, and representations to the

Commission.



     ACFCA Comments | FERC Project No. 15424-000 | Filed September 21, 2026 | Page 1
 II. COMMON TECHNICAL ISSUE ACROSS BOTH PROCEEDINGS

In its Motion to Intervene and Protest filed September 14, 2026, and its Motion for Leave to

Answer and Reply Comments filed September 21, 2026 in Docket No. P-15423-000 (Submission

ID 1792347), a copy of which is attached as Exhibit A, ACFCA raised concerns regarding the

Cook Inlet project's reliance on continuous, passive seawater circulation to dissipate a substantial

and continuous thermal load, in the absence of any thermal plume model, hydrodynamic study, or

fisheries impact assessment in the filed application. ACFCA understands from public reporting

that residents and organizations in Eastport, including the Eastport Coalition for Healthy Oceans,
have raised a substantially similar concern regarding thermal discharge from the Western Passage

project into the surrounding water column and its potential effects on local water temperature,

current dynamics, and benthic habitat supporting Eastport's working waterfront and commercial

fisheries.

ACFCA takes no position on the specific facts, tidal regime, or environmental conditions of the

Western Passage, which ACFCA understands may differ materially from those in Upper Cook

Inlet. ACFCA offers no view on the ultimate merits of the Western Passage application. ACFCA

submits these comments only to note, for the Commission's consideration, that the thermal load

and cooling design concerns raised in each proceeding appear to arise from a common project

design used by affiliated DeepGreen entities, and that the Commission's evaluation of this common

design element in one docket may be relevant to its evaluation in the other.

III. CONCLUSION

ACFCA respectfully requests that the Commission take notice of the common ownership, common

project design, and common thermal load and cooling design concerns between this proceeding

and FERC Docket No. P-15423-000, and consider the attached exhibit as part of the record in this

proceeding. ACFCA takes no position on intervention, dismissal, or any other relief requested by

other parties in this docket.




     ACFCA Comments | FERC Project No. 15424-000 | Filed September 21, 2026 | Page 2
 Respectfully submitted,

 Motion for Leave to Answer and Reply Comments: Submission ID 1792347 | Filed
September 21, 2026
                                UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
             BEFORE THE FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV, LLC                                                                  )
DeepGreen Cook Inlet Subsea-Compute &                                                          )
Infrastructure Hub Project                                                                     )

                                                                        ) Docket No. P-15423-000

       MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER AND REPLY COMMENTS OF THE
        ALASKA COMMERCIAL FISHERIES CONSERVATION ALLIANCE


Pursuant to Rule 213 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission's ("Commission" or "FERC")

Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. § 385.213, the Alaska Commercial Fisheries

Conservation Alliance ("ACFCA") moves for leave to answer and submits these Reply Comments

in response to the Answer to Motions to Intervene, Response to Protest, and Clarification of

Comments ("Answer") filed by DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV, LLC ("DeepGreen" or "Applicant")

on September 21, 2026, in the above-captioned docket.

I. MOTION FOR LEAVE TO ANSWER

Rule 213(a)(2) generally prohibits answers to protests and answers absent Commission

authorization. ACFCA requests leave to file this Reply because it will assist the Commission in

developing a complete record and will not delay this proceeding. This Reply: (a) responds to

DeepGreen's characterization of the compounded power-cooling failure condition identified in

ACFCA's Protest as a matter for the study period, and notes that the authority cited in the Answer

for that proposition cannot be verified in the Commission's published decisions; (b) identifies that

the Answer does not address the notice requirements applicable to affected municipalities and

counties under 18 C.F.R. § 4.32(a)(2); and (c) responds to factual characterizations in the Answer

regarding DeepGreen's prior contact with the Alaska Energy Authority ("AEA") and the basis for



       ACFCA Reply | FERC Docket No. P-15423-000 | Submission ID 1792347 | Page 1
 the project's stated footprint, which remain unsupported by any documentation. Good cause exists

for the Commission to accept this Reply.

II. REPLY TO DEEPGREEN'S STUDY-STAGE ARGUMENT

DeepGreen's Answer characterizes each deficiency identified in ACFCA's Protest as a matter

properly deferred to the three-year study period authorized under a preliminary permit issued

pursuant to Section 4(f) of the Federal Power Act, 16 U.S.C. § 797(f). In support, the Answer cites

FFP Missouri River, LLC, 137 FERC ¶ 61,048 (2011), and Symphony Hydro LLC, 128 FERC ¶

61,068 (2009). ACFCA's research indicates that neither citation corresponds to a genuine
Commission decision. No entity named FFP Missouri River, LLC appears in the Commission's

records; the applicants operating under the FFP name in that period were separately named and

separately docketed. Symphony Hydro, LLC is a real applicant, but its preliminary permit

application before the Commission concerned a hydrokinetic project at St. Anthony Falls in

Minneapolis, Minnesota, filed in 2015, not a 2009 proceeding, and ACFCA has found no order at

128 FERC ¶ 61,068 concerning that applicant or that project. ACFCA requests that DeepGreen

either produce the full case name, docket number, and issuance date for each authority relied upon,

so the Commission and intervenors can confirm it exists and supports the proposition asserted, or

withdraw the citations.

Independent of that citation question, ACFCA does not dispute that a preliminary permit issued

under Section 4(f) does not require final licensing-stage data. ACFCA's Protest does not rest on the

absence of final data alone. It identifies a specific, internally inconsistent design condition that the

Answer does not engage. As set forth in Section III.B of ACFCA's Protest, the project as described

relies entirely on passive seawater circulation, driven by tidal flow, to dissipate an estimated 341.2

million BTU per hour of continuous thermal load from the 66 subsea compute pods. Upper Cook

Inlet's mixed semi-diurnal tidal regime produces up to four zero-velocity slack tide periods per day.

During those same periods, the marine hydrokinetic turbine array generates no electricity. The

application thus describes a project in which the mechanism for removing heat and the mechanism


       ACFCA Reply | FERC Docket No. P-15423-000 | Submission ID 1792347 | Page 2
 for generating power fail at the same time, on a predictable and recurring basis. ACFCA's Protest

terms this the double failure condition.

DeepGreen's Answer does not deny that this condition exists and does not identify any engineering

feature of the project as filed that would address it. Instead, the Answer states that thermal

dispersion characteristics will be addressed within the formal study plan during the permit term.

ACFCA submits that this response does not meet the objection. ACFCA's Protest does not merely

ask DeepGreen to model an existing design; it identifies that no design solution to the double

failure condition has been proposed, and that available engineering responses, including battery
storage, a grid interconnection, thermal buffering capacity, or curtailment of computing load

during slack tide, would each require infrastructure, footprint, or operational characteristics

materially different from what DeepGreen filed in February 2026 and supplemented in June 2026.

A study plan developed during the permit term can determine how to solve this problem. It cannot

determine whether the project the Commission is being asked to prioritize is the project that will

ultimately be built. ACFCA renews its request that the Commission require DeepGreen to identify

its proposed engineering approach to the compounded power-cooling failure condition and the

resulting effect on project footprint before the application is processed further.

III. THE ANSWER DOES NOT ADDRESS MUNICIPAL AND COUNTY NOTICE

Section 4.32(a)(2) of the Commission's regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 4.32(a)(2), requires an applicant

for a preliminary permit to identify each city, town, or similar political subdivision in which any

part of the project would be located, each county in which any part of the project would be located,

and each other political subdivision in the general area of the project likely to be interested in or

affected by the application. DeepGreen's Answer responds to the motions to intervene filed by the

Kenai Peninsula Borough ("KPB"), the Center for Biological Diversity, and ACFCA, and responds

to ACFCA's Protest on the merits described above. The Answer does not address whether the

notice required by Section 4.32(a)(2) was provided to KPB or to any other affected local

government. ACFCA understands KPB to have raised this issue in its own filing. Because notice


       ACFCA Reply | FERC Docket No. P-15423-000 | Submission ID 1792347 | Page 3
 under Section 4.32(a)(2) is a procedural requirement distinct from the study-stage merits the

Answer addresses, ACFCA requests that the Commission require DeepGreen to confirm

compliance with that section directly.

IV. THE ANSWER'S FACTUAL CLARIFICATIONS ARE UNSUPPORTED

DeepGreen's Answer offers two factual characterizations relevant to ACFCA's Protest without

accompanying documentation. First, regarding the Alaska Energy Authority, the Answer states

that DeepGreen has conducted standard preliminary stakeholder and regulatory inquiries

customary for early-stage project concepts, and has not executed a formal binding partnership, co-
sponsorship, or formal agency agreement with AEA. This characterization does not identify the

nature, date, or content of any communication with AEA, and does not respond to the basis for

ACFCA's belief, stated in its Protest, that the application misrepresented the nature of that

relationship. ACFCA renews its request that the Commission require DeepGreen to produce the

substance of any correspondence or communication with AEA referenced or relied upon in the

application.

Second, regarding project footprint, the Answer characterizes the turbine counts and boundary

envelope identified in the application as a conservative study corridor and states that the final

operational array footprint will be substantially smaller. ACFCA has no basis in the current record

to evaluate that assertion, which is not accompanied by any engineering analysis, siting rationale,

or comparison between the filed footprint and the anticipated final footprint. Until such support is

provided, ACFCA submits that the Commission and affected parties are entitled to evaluate the

application, including its fisheries and navigational impacts, based on the footprint as filed rather

than an undocumented representation that it will later be reduced.

V. REQUEST FOR FURTHER DEFICIENCY CORRESPONDENCE

ACFCA requests that Commission Staff issue further deficiency correspondence to DeepGreen

requiring, at a minimum: (a) identification of DeepGreen's proposed engineering approach, if any,



       ACFCA Reply | FERC Docket No. P-15423-000 | Submission ID 1792347 | Page 4
 to the compounded power-cooling failure condition described in Section II above, and its effect on

project footprint and infrastructure; (b) confirmation of compliance with the notice requirements of

18 C.F.R. § 4.32(a)(2); (c) the full case name, docket number, and issuance date for the two

decisions cited in Section II of the Answer, given that ACFCA's own research has not located either

decision as cited, or withdrawal of those citations; and (d) documentation supporting the factual

characterizations in Section III of DeepGreen's Answer regarding communications with the Alaska

Energy Authority and the basis for the stated project footprint. ACFCA does not request that the

Commission resolve these issues on the present record. It requests only that DeepGreen be required
to substantiate the representations made in its Answer to the same extent the Answer asks the

Commission and intervenors to rely on them.

VI. CONCLUSION

For the foregoing reasons, ACFCA requests that the Commission grant this Motion for Leave to

Answer, accept the accompanying Reply Comments, and require DeepGreen to respond to the

specific matters identified herein before further action is taken on the preliminary permit

application.


Respectfully submitted,
